title: Does Butter Have Lactose? Much Less Than You Might Think

seo.title: Does Butter Have Lactose? How Much
seo.meta_description: Yes, but very little. Churning cream removes much of the watery phase where lactose is dissolved, so a normal serving of butter contains only a small amount.
seo.search_intent: Explain why butter is low in lactose and how that relates to lactose intolerance.

excerpt: Butter can contain trace or small amounts of lactose, but far less than milk. Churning concentrates milk fat and removes much of the watery phase where lactose is dissolved, so a normal serving contributes very little lactose.
content_html:
Butter is made from dairy, but it does not keep the roughly 12 grams of lactose found in a cup of milk. Lactose is mostly dissolved in the watery portion of milk, while butter concentrates the fat.

Churning separates fat from liquid

When cream is churned, fat globules join and much of the liquid leaves as buttermilk. Finished butter is at least about 80% fat and contains relatively little water, so little lactose remains.

Many butter products contain less than 1 gram of lactose per 100 grams, making the amount in a tablespoon only a small fraction of a gram. Many people with lactose intolerance tolerate that dose.

Tolerance is still individual

Lactose intolerance is dose-dependent. Someone who is very sensitive may prefer a specifically lactose-free butter or clarified butter, which contains even fewer milk solids.

This does not make butter safe for milk allergy

Butter can still contain milk proteins. Low lactose is not the same as absence of milk allergens.

faq.question: How much lactose is in butter?
faq.answer: Many butters contain less than 1 gram per 100 grams, so a tablespoon contains only a very small fraction of a gram.

faq.question: Does ghee have less lactose?
faq.answer: Usually yes because water and milk solids are further removed, though exact residual amounts depend on the product.

faq.question: Is butter safe for milk allergy?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. It may still contain milk proteins despite very little lactose.
